tagline: All-in-one platform for selling and delivering online courses.
verdictSummary: Selling and delivering one course — a landing page, hosted checkout, a magic-link login, a folder of gated lessons — is a real multi-day build. What doesn't come with it is Kajabi's actual breadth: a whole stack of site, community, email automation, funnels, and analytics bundled into one subscription.
coreLoopDIY: A landing page with hosted checkout, a magic-link login for buyers, and a folder of Markdown lessons served as a gated, ordered course.
whatYouLose: the all-in-one stack, replaced by several separately maintained pieces
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay to avoid stitching together and maintaining a dozen separate creator-business tools — the value is having one system, not any single feature inside it.
notes: The high price makes DIY attractive; the actual breadth of the platform is what makes a full replacement genuinely hard.
prompt:
Build a one-course sales-and-delivery site — deliberately scoped to one product at one price, not a general platform. A landing page with the course pitch and curriculum, and a buy button that goes straight to a hosted checkout (Stripe Checkout is the simplest option). A webhook from the payment provider marks the buyer enrolled and emails them a magic sign-in link — no passwords, just a link that logs them in. Course content lives as a folder of Markdown lessons (with embedded video, either self-hosted or an unlisted link to a video host), rendered as an ordered lesson list with a per-student completion checkbox on each one. Keep a students table recording email, purchase date, and lessons completed. Add a small admin view, not public-facing, showing enrollments, a revenue total, and a way to grant a student free access by hand.

Do not build email marketing automations, community features, funnels, or a multi-course catalog — those are the actual breadth Kajabi sells, and stitching them all in is real, ongoing scope well past a personal course site.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Kajabi course and students?
faq.a: The lesson content, largely yes — copy your videos and text into the Markdown lesson structure. Student and purchase history generally doesn't export cleanly, since it's tied to Kajabi's own billing records.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The landing page and lesson viewer are both responsive web pages, so yes for browsing and watching. There's no dedicated mobile app or offline video download.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a database, typically a few dollars a month, plus standard payment-processing fees on sales — no per-month platform fee at all beyond that.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The bundle. Kajabi's real value is site, course delivery, email, community, and analytics all working together as one system; this build gives you one solid course page, not the other four things.
